- Give an element a container name and declare that it should be a size container using container-type (or the shorthand container):

- Ensure that the element actually has a size (it must establish a containing box whose inline/block dimensions can be measured).

  - the container’s type (size queries do not necessarily need a name if you use the default container context described in the guide),
  and then specify a size condition such as width >= ... or inline-size >= ... to respond to the container’s size.

2. Difference between size and style queries (from main guide and container-type)
- Size queries:
  - React to the container’s physical dimensions (inline-size, block-size, width, height, etc.).
  - Depend on the container-type declaring that the element participates as a size container (for example, container-type: inline-size; or container-type: size;).

- Style queries:
  - React to styles of the container (for example, whether a given custom property or computed style has some value) rather than its physical size.
  - Depend on declaring the element as a style container (for example, container-type: style; or container-type: size style; depending on the syntax shown on MDN).
  - Conditions in @container use style() or related style query syntax to match based on style values instead of dimensions.

3. Container query length units and what each measures (from <length> CSS type page, “Container query length units” section)
The "Container query length units" subsection lists the units explicitly as links:
- cqw – a container query width unit.
- cqh – a container query height unit.
- cqi – a container query inline-size unit.
- cqb – a container query block-size unit.
- cqmin – a container query minimum size unit.
- cqmax – a container query maximum size unit.

- 1cqw: 1% of the query container’s width.
- 1cqh: 1% of the query container’s height.
- 1cqi: 1% of the query container’s inline size (the dimension along the inline axis, which depends on writing mode).
- 1cqb: 1% of the query container’s block size (the dimension along the block axis).
- 1cqmin: 1% of the smaller of the query container’s width/height (or inline/block sizes).
- 1cqmax: 1% of the larger of the query container’s width/height (or inline/block sizes).

This list of all six units (cqw, cqh, cqi, cqb, cqmin, cqmax) and the description that they are container query length units is visible in the "Container query length units" section of the <length> page, where each unit appears as its own link.

- Do not rely solely on cqw/cqh/cqi/cqb/cqmin/cqmax for critical layout if you need to support browsers that lack these units.
- Provide a more widely supported length first, then override it with container query units inside a feature‑supported context. In practice, this means:
  - Use a baseline layout using regular lengths (px, em, rem, % or viewport units) that works everywhere.
  - Use @supports (width: 1cqw) (or a similar feature query) or container feature detection recommended in the guide to layer on container-query-unit-based enhancements only in browsers that support them.
- Keep in mind that container query units are tied to the container’s size; if they are not supported, the browser will ignore those declarations, so you must ensure that the previous, broadly-supported declarations still produce a usable layout.
